papers.title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
papers.authors: Wang Wen-quan, Ting Du, Jiangxia Ye, Xiaohong Huang, Yangyang Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors. papers.title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
papers.authors: Davide Martinetti, Laura Erbetta, Danièle Bevacqua, Olivier Bonnefon, Marino Gatto
papers.abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. papers.title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
papers.authors: Toni M. Withers, Andrew R. Pugh, Darryl A. Herron, Dean Satchell, Shaun Wilkinson
papers.source: OpenAlex / New Zealand Journal of Zoology
papers.abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. This sequence of events leading to finding an established population highlights the potential for citizen science observations and eDNA monitoring to both uncover and pinpoint a cryptic pest's location as part of biosecurity surveillance.

papers.title: Sensitivity evaluation and multi-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field
papers.authors: Kunyang Ju, Zhifan Ma, Shuhan Guo, YuKe Wang, Shengnan Dong
papers.abstract: Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease (PWD), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate (EB) is the main nematicide for trunk injection. Nevertheless, long-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL (320.99 μg•mL -1 ) and CD strains (114.63 μg•mL -1 ), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio (PL vs CD) of 2.8 < 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B. xylophilus populations in Shandong. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Invasive alien plants (IAP) can threaten biodiversity by disrupting trophic interactions and, consequently, affect agroecosystems by providing alternative resources for phytophagous insects at crop field margins. This may influence pest populations and parasitoid performance through bottom‐up effects. We examined the cascading effects of three IAPs common at agroecosystem interfaces ( Galinsoga quadriradiata , Reynoutria japonica , Senecio inaequidens ) on a major pest, the black bean aphid ( Aphis fabae ), and its parasitoid Aphidius colemani , a widely used biological control agent. We assessed key life‐history traits to evaluate both aphid host and parasitoid fitness, choosing Beta vulgaris as the control crop‐plant, a cultivated host plant commonly infested by Aphis fabae , used here to compare the other effects relative to it. The traits evaluated here were aphid host mass and larviposition rate, parasitism ratio, parasitoid emergence ratio, parasitic success, female ratio, development time, mass, tibia length and egg load. papers.title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
papers.authors: Niamjit Das, Kevin Andrew
papers.abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. papers.abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. A very specific predator, Rhizophagus grandis (Coleoptera, Monotomidae), has followed its prey in its territorial expansion, with temporal and spatial lags due to long distance passive transportation of D. micans with trade, and to habitat fragmentation. When both species coexist, D. micans is very sparce and only occasionally kills trees, because the high capacity of R. grandis to locate prey even at very low densities enables it to control the pest. This very particular relationship has been exploited for biological control. Mass production and inoculative releases of R. grandis have been undertaken in four countries: Georgia since 1963, France (1978), Great Britain (1983) and Türkiye (1985). papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: Farida B. Gabdrakhmanova, Ekaterina S. Churbanova, S. Е. Solovieva, Антипин Игорь Сергеевич
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.title: Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network Architecture with Attention-Guided Feature Refinement for Robust Image Classification
papers.authors: KRISHNA SANDEEP JONNALA, K VENKAT RAJU
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Image classification remains a foundational problem in computer vision, underpinning applications that range from medical diagnostics to autonomous navigation. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have substantially advanced classification accuracy over the last decade, standard architectures such as VGG, ResNet, and plain CNNs often struggle to jointly optimize accuracy, parameter efficiency, and robustness to intra-class variation. This paper proposes an AttentionGuided Refinement Network (AGR-Net), a CNN architecture that integrates a lightweight channel-and-spatial attention module with residual feature refinement blocks to improve discriminative feature learning while maintaining a compact parameter footprint. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset using a rigorous experimental protocol that includes data augmentation, learning-rate scheduling, and five-fold cross-validation. papers.abstract: The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven solutions across connected systems. However, these domains face persistent challenges such as heterogeneous datasets, limited labeled data, real-time processing constraints, privacy concerns, model interpretability, and poor generalization across environments. This review examines the application of major Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for solving classification, prediction, optimization, anomaly detection, routing, image analysis, and decision-support problems. The empirical patterns across the literature are summarized cautiously across studies. General lessons that emerged across the reviewed domains were also presented. Overall, the review provides researchers with a concise foundation for understanding current AI methods, their practical limitations, and future research directions in the aspect of connected environments. This article has tried to clarify various aspects and overall issues related to the use of AI techniques in computer networks, image processing and computer vision, smart agriculture and related intelligent systems. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). papers.title: Application of medical gases in prevention and treatment of electromagnetic radiation injury.
papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. papers.abstract: Bacterial fruit blotch (BFB), caused by Acidovorax citrulli, severely limits watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) production. Concerns about environmental pollution, pathogen resistance, and food safety associated with synthetic bactericides highlight the need for sustainable management alternatives. This study evaluated the combined effects of botanical extracts and varietal selection on BFB suppression and watermelon yield in the Guinea Savannah agroecological zone of Taraba State, Nigeria. Field experiments were conducted at Wukari and Ardo Kola during the 2020 and 2021 cropping seasons using a 4 × 5 factorial arrangement in a randomized complete block design with three replications. Four varieties—Sugar Baby, Charleston Gray, Crimson Sweet, and Kaolack—were evaluated under five treatments: neem (Azadirachta indica) extract, jatropha (Jatropha curcas) extract, combined neem and jatropha extracts, copper hydroxide, and an untreated control. papers.title: Towards digital agriculture: uncovering the drivers and barriers to the adoption of digital agricultural technologies
papers.authors: Xinrui Gao, Yangyang Zheng, Rumiao Li
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
papers.abstract: Accurately identifying the driving and hindering factors of agricultural digital technology adoption is the key to overcoming the “last mile” challenge in agricultural technology diffusion. Based on the evolutionary game theory of scale-free complex networks, this paper constructs an actor network for agricultural technology adoption to analyze its multidimensional mechanisms of influence in depth. The results indicate that while government subsidies provide short-term incentives for technology diffusion, their sustainability is limited. Agricultural technology advantages serve as the core driver, transforming exogenous technology into an endogenous growth engine. Conversely, the information gap, the perception of high risk, and high costs hinder farmers’ willingness to adopt these technologies. This study expands the application boundaries of complex network theory in agricultural technology adoption, reveals the operational laws governing driving and hindering factors, and provides a valuable reference for optimizing agricultural technology adoption strategies.

Methods The primary data were collected through in-depth interviews with 30 participants, including organic farmers, community leaders, and local agricultural officials. papers.abstract: Postharvest diseases remain among the most critical factors limiting the shelf life, quality, and marketability of fresh produce worldwide, contributing substantially to economic losses and food insecurity. Although conventional preservation strategies such as synthetic fungicides and low-temperature storage have been effective, their long-term use is increasingly constrained by pathogen resistance, chemical residue concerns, environmental impacts, and stricter regulatory controls. In recent years, probiotic microorganisms and biological control agents (BCAs), particularly when incorporated into edible coating systems, have emerged as promising and bio-based approaches for postharvest disease management. These bio-based systems provide multifunctional benefits by integrating direct antimicrobial activity with competitive exclusion of pathogens, induction of host defense responses, and modulation of fruit physiological processes, while simultaneously forming protective barriers that regulate gas exchange and moisture loss. papers.title: RNA Interference for Precision Management of Plant-Parasitic Nematodes: Mechanisms, Delivery Constraints and Translational Evidence
papers.authors: Vadaga Dhanasri, Swadhin Kumar Swain, Rudraboyina Sai Kiran, Huzaifah Ashaq, Sukriti Saha
papers.source: OpenAlex / PLANT CELL BIOTECHNOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
papers.abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes are persistent constraints on crop productivity because their behaviour, protected habitats and intimate relationships with host roots complicate both diagnosis and control. RNA interference offers sequence-guided suppression of nematode gene expression without requiring a conventional toxicant to act on a broad physiological target. Yet molecular specificity should not be conflated with biological control, and promising experiments have produced uneven results across species, life stages, delivery systems and scales. This critical narrative review examines research on double-stranded RNA exposure, target validation, host-induced gene silencing, artificial microRNAs, non-transgenic formulations, nanocarriers and translation to field use. Peer-reviewed experimental and methodological studies published through 14 August 2026 were considered, with seminal earlier work included to establish the mechanism. The strongest evidence concerns gene knockdown and reduced infection or reproduction in controlled plant systems, particularly root-knot and cyst nematodes. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Today, soil pollution with heavy metals and petroleum compounds is one of the main environmental problems. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. This reframes a persistent gap in philosophy of mind: qualia have long been debated while the physical architecture that must bound it has been neglected. papers.abstract: Introduction Drug-resistant fungal infections remain a major clinical challenge, and antifungal adjuvants offer a promising strategy to restore azole efficacy. This study investigated whether usnic acid (UA), which lacks intrinsic antifungal activity, enhances the activity of itraconazole (ITR), voriconazole (VOR), posaconazole (POS), isavuconazole (ISA), and fluconazole (FLU) against clinically relevant fungal pathogens. Methods The synergistic effects of UA combined with each azole were evaluated against clinical isolates of Aspergillus spp. ( n = 64), Candida spp. ( n = 24), Exophiala dermatitidis ( n = 14), and Cryptococcus neoformans ( n = 8) using CLSI-standardized broth microdilution and checkerboard assays. According to their clinical use, ISA was tested against molds, whereas FLU was tested against Candida spp. and C. neoformans . Interactions were classified by the fractional inhibitory concentration index as synergy (FICI ≤ 0.5), indifference (0.5 < FICI ≤ 4.0), or antagonism (FICI > 4.0). papers.title: Recent plant photosynthate as a driver of ecological and evolutionary processes
papers.authors: David Johnson, Hannah M. Griffiths
papers.abstract: Summary Plants rapidly allocate carbon from photosynthesis belowground via root exudates and root‐associated microorganisms. Here we synthesise recent evidence of our understanding of the consequences of this ‘fast’ pathway of recent photosynthate flux for major ecological and evolutionary processes. This rapid input of plant‐derived carbon to soils shapes food webs and drives processes including soil CO 2 efflux, nutrient cycling, plant community dynamics, stability of symbioses and evolution of contrasting modes of nutrition, such as parasitism and mycoheterotrophy. We also highlight how seasonality and anthropogenic and natural perturbations likely determine the magnitude and dynamics of this fast pathway across major vegetation types, but these factors remain understudied. Further gaps in understanding include demonstrating causal links between photosynthate flow and key biogeochemical cycling processes and the capture of photosynthate by co‐occurring root‐associated microorganisms.

papers.title: Global Research Trends in Tick-Borne Diseases of Livestock: A Bibliometric Analysis
papers.abstract: Tick-borne diseases (TBDs) are a critical limitation of livestock health and productivity on the international arena as they result in huge economic losses and emerging challenges due to changing environmental conditions.The objective of the current study was to examine the current trends in the world in terms of the research on tickborne livestock diseases through the use of bibliometric methodology.A structured search strategy was used to retrieve publications indexed in PubMed database between 2020 and 2026 and 2,405 records were included in the analysis.The place of bibliometric analysis was conducted with the help of Bibliometrix (R 4.5.2) and VOSviewer to assess the trends of publications, top contributors, collaboration networks, and theme development.The findings revealed a more or less fluctuating but generally speaking increasing pattern in scientific production with the highest production expected in 2025.China, Brazil and the United States were found to be the most prolific nations with some of the most renowned research institutions like Obihiro University of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine and Universidade Federal de Goiás in the center stage.Through co-authorship

papers.title: Resource subsidies mediated by non-native species: a review
papers.authors: Letícia Alves, Janeide de Assis Guilherme Padilha, Phillip Joschka Haubrock, Amanda L. Subalusky, Ronaldo Sousa
papers.abstract: Non-native species are recognized as one of the major drivers of biodiversity change globally, with profound impacts on ecosystem functions and services. Despite the high number of studies on non-native species published, mainly in the last two decades, an often-overlooked aspect is their role as mediators of resource subsidies (the cross-boundary movement of energy, nutrients, or materials). This topic may have theoretical and empirical implications because non-native species may play a major role in ecosystem connectivity by transporting—or interrupting the transport of—energy and organic matter. Therefore, the main aims of this review were to (1) assess temporal trends, geographic distribution, and methodological approaches in research on resource subsidies mediated by non-native species; (2) synthesize how non-native species alter the magnitude, direction, and dynamics of resource subsidies across ecosystems and their implications for ecosystem functioning; and (3) identify key gaps in current knowledge and define future research priorities.
